newsitem.title: USA: Police, Customs inspectors nabbed in Miami drug case.
newsitem.headline: Police, Customs inspectors nabbed in Miami drug case.

text.p: Two veteran U.S. Customs inspectors and three Florida police officers used their badges to cash in on the drug trade, the Miami U.S. Attorney's Office said on Thursday.

Authorities said a nine-month corruption probe found that the five were involved in schemes to spirit drug shipments through Miami International Airport, provide escorts to smugglers and participate in drug and cash rip-offs.
They surrendered on Thursday on conspiracy, extortion and robbery charges and were released on bail. Officials said all had agreed to plead guilty and would be sentenced at a future date.
Customs Deputy Commissioner Sam Banks said the Customs Service was betrayed by the inspectors.

"We feel that this tars our organisation," said Banks, who travelled from Washington D.C. to Miami to announce the charges and to speak to Customs employees in Miami, a key frontier in the U.S. war on drug smuggling.
"We probably make more seizures here than anywhere in the country. Our integrity is important to us," he said.

Customs Inspector Edwin Perez Martinez, 51, Hallandale police Sergeant John Salazar, 37, and officers Gilberto Hernandez, 31, and Thomas Murphy, 34, were charged with conspiracy to commit robbery and extortion. Martinez and Hernandez also were charged with robbery and extortion, and Murphy and Salazar faced separate extortion charges.
Hallandale is a municipality in Broward County, just south of Fort Lauderdale.
In a separate allegation, Customs Inspector Angel Ruiz, 36, was charged with attempted extortion.
Two other Customs inspectors resigned as a result of the investigation and another was suspended, officials said.
In one instance, Martinez, a 25-year Customs veteran, altered computer records to clear a 660-pound (300 kg) shipment of cocaine through MIA to a business called Lobster Depot, officials said.

Hernandez, under guise of a legitimate police raid, then stole 580 pounds (263 kg) of cocaine from a Lobster Depot warehouse with Murphy acting as lookout. The cocaine was sold, with Hernandez and Martinez receiving over $300,000 and Murphy getting more than $50,000 from the proceeds, officials said.

Authorities alleged that Ruiz, a 13-year Customs veteran, took $10,000 cash and a Rolex watch to escort someone posing as a smuggler and carrying two kilos, or about four and a-half pounds, of heroin through Customs at Miami's airport.
